title: query_graph input
description: An escape hatch for a question the typed tools do not answer in one call: one bounded, read-only openCypher query over the snapshot (extra profile). Try find_symbols, get_relationships, trace_paths and analyze_impact first; they add dispatch, candidates and boundaries this does not. MATCH and OPTIONAL MATCH node and relationship patterns, variable-length paths with an upper bound of at most limits.max_depth, 6 by default and 12 at most, for the whole query (*1..3), WHERE, WITH, RETURN, ORDER BY, SKIP, LIMIT, count and collect. Labels are symbol kinds, file and external; relationship types are the snapshot's (calls, imports, implements, references, ...). Writes, procedures and file access are refused. Rows are `name path:line`, tagged inferred when a hop is.

repository_id.description: Optional when exactly one repository is registered.

snapshot_id.description: Null pins the current published snapshot.

query.description: The query, such as MATCH (c)-[r:calls]->(t:function {name: $name}) WHERE NOT c.test RETURN r. Grammar: docs/proofmesh/mcp.md.

params.description: Values for $name parameters, passed apart from the text and never spliced into it.

freshness.description: snapshot (default) answers from the published snapshot. strict first checks that the working tree is exactly what the snapshot was built from; if not, it starts an index and refuses with STALE_INPUT naming the changed files.

envelope.description: lean, the default over MCP: plain text with no JSON and no structuredContent. A header `# <tool> · <n> rows · <snapshot> current` (stale when the snapshot is older than the repository's current one), one `<name> <path>:<line>` row per result, then `# ` lines for the limitations of this answer and `# more: cursor <c>` when a next page exists. The line is the call, import or reference site for relationship, impact and path rows and the declaration for symbol rows; tags follow: in or out when both directions are asked, depth=<n>, dispatch, external, candidate, ambiguous, unresolved:<reason>, and the relationship type when the query mixes types. A name or path with a space, quote or # is quoted as JSON. For query_graph, the header also names the snapshot's commit (`# query_graph · commit <sha> · <n> rows · ...`); each row is its first node, relationship or path (a path a row per node, depth=<n>), the other columns as column=value tags, then inferred when any hop is inferred. compact: the JSON envelope without the snapshot-wide parts an earlier answer gave (coverage, unresolved reasons, standing limitations). full: the whole JSON envelope. Ask for compact or full for ids, evidence and totals.
